official.deadline_note: Stage 2 is by invitation only and closes on 18 October 2026; the open-call Stage 1 deadline for the 2027/28 cycle closed on 26 July 2026, and the official applicants page now states that applications for 2027/28 are closed for the Africa, Latin America, SIDS and Asia streams. The next open Stage 1 window is expected around June/July. Stage-level dates for the Latin America and SIDS strands were not confirmed.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle (awards commencing August/September 2027); a recurring three-stage annual cycle
official.status_note: The official applicants page states: "Applications for 2027/28 are now closed for the Africa, Latin America, SIDS, and Asia streams." For the 2027/28 cycle the Africa and Asia Stage 1 guidance notes set: Stage 1 preliminary applications opened 29 June 2026 and closed 26 July 2026; Stage 2 detailed applications (by invitation only) open 21 September 2026 and close 18 October 2026; Stage 3 interviews take place in November and December 2026; award confirmation follows in June/early July 2027 for study commencing August or September 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award includes the payment of academic fees. The programme overview states the fellowship offers "the opportunity to undertake a fully funded one-year master's level programme at a higher education institution (HEI) in Ireland" and that "the award covers programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs".
benefits: Payment of visa application fees; medical and travel insurance; economy flights to and from Ireland; and the Irish residence permit fee
A settling-in allowance towards items needed on arrival in Ireland
A completion and departure allowance at the end of the study period
A monthly living stipend of €700 (subject to review)

Student accommodation arranged and paid for trimesters 1 and 2 (normally September to May), and in trimester 3 a monthly accommodation stipend of €800-€1000 depending on location in Ireland (subject to review)
eligibility: Be a resident national of an eligible country under the relevant strand (Africa: Angola, Burundi, DR Congo, Djibouti, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe; Asia: Vietnam, Cambodia, Lao PDR; SIDS: listed African, Asian, Caribbean and Pacific small island developing states; Latin America: Central America Award, Cecilia Grierson Award and Roger Casement Award countries)
Have a minimum of two or three years' substantial work experience directly relevant to the proposed programme(s) of study, depending on country

Hold a bachelor's level academic qualification from an accredited and government-recognised higher education institution, with a minimum grade point average of 3.0 (4.0 scale) - a first class honour or second class honour Grade 1, awarded in 2015 or later (a second class honour Grade 2 may be accepted with substantial directly relevant work experience)
Not already hold a qualification at master's level or higher, and not currently be undertaking or due to start a master's level programme in the academic year 2026/27
Be applying to commence a new programme at master's level in Ireland no sooner than August 2027, and be in a position to take up the Fellowship in the academic year 2027/2028

Demonstrate leadership abilities and aspirations, a commitment to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals within your own country, and a commitment to contribute to building positive relationships with Ireland; have selected three relevant programmes from the Directory of Eligible Programmes; and must not have applied to the Ireland Fellows Programme on more than one previous occasion
requirements: Meet all eligibility criteria for the relevant strand
Secure an eligible master's level place at an Irish higher education institution (HEI application fees are paid by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade for shortlisted Candidates)
Complete all three stages of the annual application process: preliminary application, detailed application, interviews

Hold an English language certificate at the required standard, or take the required test: most Irish HEIs require IELTS 6.5 overall, and shortlisted applicants without certification take the Duolingo English Test (score of 120 with at least 105 in each sub-score), or an IELTS exam in January 2027 if the course or HEI does not accept Duolingo
Apply only through the Embassy of Ireland responsible for your country, or the designated channel for your country
documents: Official identification: the passport identity page, or another form of certified official identification if you do not have a passport
Undergraduate degree award certificate and final degree academic transcripts, including the explanation of the grading system where provided
Two letters from academic referees on official letterhead with contact details and original signatures, from academics who have taught you personally (Stage 2)
One recent passport-sized photograph, a copy of the graduation certificate and transcripts for all higher education qualifications completed, and your current C.V. (Stage 2)
Original IELTS score report dated September 2025 or later, if available; results of another accepted English language test may also be included (Stage 2)

Certified hard copies bearing the official stamp and signature of the certifying authority at or prior to the interview, with certified true English translations where originals are not in English (Stage 3)
selection_criteria: A commitment to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals within your own country
A commitment to contribute to building positive relationships with Ireland
Substantial work experience directly relevant to the proposed programme(s) of study
Academic record at bachelor's level, with a minimum grade point average of 3.0 (4.0 scale)
The quality of the statement on why you wish to be considered for a Fellowship in Ireland, which the guidance note describes as a critical factor in how the application is scored
coverage: Visa application fees, medical and travel insurance, and the Irish residence permit fee
A settling-in allowance and a completion and departure allowance
application_method: Stage 1 - preliminary application: typed and submitted by email to the relevant Embassy of Ireland, with the application form as a .docx or PDF and supporting documents as separate PDF attachments
Stage 2 - detailed application: by invitation from the Embassy, submitted by email with all required documents
Stage 3 - interview: in person or remotely by video or telephone conference, in November and December 2026
Applications must be personal to the applicant; using someone else's work or content generated by AI tools is not permitted
official.application_route: Apply by email to the Embassy of Ireland responsible for your country (Ghana applies online at irelandfellows.africa; Lesotho and Zimbabwe via the Canon Collins link), then progress through the invitation-only Stage 2 and Stage 3 stages
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be a resident national of an eligible country for the relevant strand; for the SIDS strand, applicants must be a national of an eligible SIDS country and resident in an eligible SIDS country, which may be a different country in the same region
official.international_eligibility: Open only to nationals of the eligible countries listed for each strand; it is not open to Irish nationals or to nationals of non-eligible countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Programmes must be selected from the Ireland Fellows Programme Directory of Eligible Programmes, with three ranked choices. In the Africa strand, applications in Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Eritrea, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan and Zambia are by invitation only, restricted to staff of government departments and NGOs working in partnership with Irish Aid and personnel of organisations aligned with Irish Aid's development strategy that have already been identified by the Embassy; applications from outside these partnerships will not be eligible
official.duration: One year; depending on the programme, between 10 and 16 months, with the academic year running from September/October 2027 to June-September 2028
official.description: The Irish Government offers fellowship programmes to students from developing countries to undertake full-time study at Master's level at an Irish higher education institution, focused on courses that build capacity to deliver the Sustainable Development Goals in the Fellow's home country. The programme is fully funded by the Irish Government and is offered under the auspices of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and is managed by the relevant Embassy responsible for the applicant's eligible country.
official.region: Europe - study in Ireland; open to applicants from eligible countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Small Island Developing States
official.program_type: One-year master's level programme at a higher education institution (HEI) in Ireland
official.english_requirement: Irish higher education institutions require an IELTS certificate or equivalent, with most HEIs requiring a score of 6.5 overall and some requiring a higher overall score or specific band scores. Shortlisted applicants who do not yet hold the required certification take the Duolingo English Test (a score of 120 with at least 105 in each sub-score); if the course or HEI does not accept Duolingo, an IELTS exam in January 2027 is required. An IELTS test is only valid if completed in September 2025 or later.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-package award rather than a stipend: academic fees, flights both ways, insurance, visa and residence-permit fees, and accommodation for the first two trimesters are all paid, on top of a €700 monthly living stipend, so the money you need on hand is mainly for settling-in extras and any rent shortfall in trimester 3. You cannot apply straight to an Irish university - you must first be shortlisted by the Embassy of Ireland, and only then are you invited to apply to Irish HEIs, choosing from two programmes with the Department paying those application fees. The calendar is long and conditional, running from Stage 1 in June/July through interviews in November/December to confirmations the following June, so your degree date, English test validity window and passport expiry all need to be lined up months ahead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early to mid-career professionals in eligible partner countries who already hold a relevant bachelor's degree, can show two to three years of directly relevant work, and want a fully funded one-year taught master's tied to SDG capacity-building at home.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears under a specific strand and email the relevant Embassy of Ireland to ask whether that country runs an open call or is invitation-only before you invest time in the form.
Check your bachelor's award date (must be 2015 or later) and your result against the 3.0/4.0 minimum, and obtain the grading-system explanation that goes with your transcript.
Download the current Directory of Eligible Programmes and shortlist three programmes, ideally at three different HEIs, noting the academic and English entry requirements of each.
Only book an English test if your existing result is older than September 2025 - a stale certificate will not carry you through the cycle.
Prepare the Stage 1 attachments as three separately named PDF scans (passport page, degree certificate, transcript) alongside a typed Word or PDF application form.
Approach two academics who taught you personally now and ask for signed reference letters on official letterhead; they are only needed at Stage 2 but typically take weeks to obtain.
common_rejection_risks: Applying from an invitation-only country without a nomination from a pre-identified partner organisation - the guidance note states these applications will not be eligible.
Applying directly to an Irish HEI before being invited; applications should not be made until invited, so early applications waste your own fees and time.
Missing the English requirement: shortlisted Candidates who do not reach the standard for their chosen programmes in the January 2027 test have their fellowship application concluded.
Receiving no offer from either of the two invited HEI applications, which also concludes the application - so the three ranked choices must be realistic for your transcript and work history.
Hard eligibility fails that end things at Stage 1: an IELTS dated before September 2025, a bachelor's awarded before 2015, an existing master's qualification, or a second previous application.

Ranking programme choices you cannot commit to: with more than one offer you must accept your highest-ranked programme, and choices cannot be changed after Stage 2 except in exceptional circumstances.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Academic fees, return flights, accommodation for trimesters 1 and 2, visa and residence-permit fees, insurance, a settling-in allowance, a completion and departure allowance and a €700 monthly living stipend are all covered. You would still fund personal and day-to-day costs beyond that stipend, any third-trimester rent above the €800-€1,000 monthly accommodation stipend, and any dependant costs - the fellowship covers the recipient only and provides no financial support or visas for spouses or dependants. The published pages do not state who pays for an English test, so budget for one.
document_audit: The passport identity page, degree certificate and transcript must be separate PDF attachments - combining the passport and transcript into a single scan makes the application invalid.
File names must follow the Embassy's format (for example Your Name - Passport, Your Name - Undergraduate degree certificate, Your Name - Academic Transcript).
Reference letters must come from academics who taught you personally, on official letterhead, with contact details and original signatures; a line manager's letter does not qualify.
Certified hard copies stamped and signed by the certifying authority are required at or before the interview, and photocopies of certified documents are not accepted.
Original documents that are not in English need certified true English translations at Stage 3.
If your passport expires before December 2028 you will be asked for a new one once shortlisted after Stage 3, so renew well before the interview.
alerts: The open Stage 1 window is short - roughly four weeks in June/July - and the 2027/28 round is already closed, so watch the official pages from June for the next cycle.
Stage 2 is invitation-only and the 2027/28 window closes on 18 October 2026; shortlisted applicants should treat that as their hard deadline.

In the invitation-only African countries only staff of pre-identified partner government departments and NGOs are eligible, so contact the Embassy or your employer early to establish whether you are on the list.
The cycle is long and conditional: you can clear Stage 2 and the interview and still exit at the HEI offer stage or on the January 2027 English test.
Some routes are not the Embassy at all - Ghana applies online through irelandfellows.africa, while Lesotho and Zimbabwe apply through the Canon Collins link.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Stage 1 is emailed to the responsible Embassy of Ireland as a typed form with separately named PDF attachments; Stage 2 arrives by invitation through the same email route with the full document set; Stage 3 is an interview in person or by video or telephone, after which successful candidates are invited to apply to two Irish HEIs with the Department paying the application fees.
